evidence.quote: This Subcontract is governed by the laws of the State of California.
evidence.rationale: Section 17.1 selects California law.

evidence.quote: This Section is a pay-when-paid provision regulating the timing of payment. It is not a condition precedent to Contractor's obligation to pay, and it does not shift to Subcontractor the risk of Owner's nonpayment.
evidence.rationale: Section 7.3 ties timing to Owner payment and expressly disclaims a condition precedent.

evidence.quote: within seven (7) days after Contractor receives payment from Owner for that Subcontract Work.
evidence.rationale: Section 7.3 states 7 days after Contractor's receipt of Owner payment. Exhibit C matches.

evidence.quote: The parties agree in writing that Contractor's receipt of payment from Owner fixes the time at which payment to Subcontractor becomes due.
evidence.rationale: A specific 7-day period is written into Section 7.3.
Section 6.1 refers to the rate stated in Exhibit C. Exhibit C's Retention rate row states 5%, which is 500 bps. Reading the rate requires combining the body with the exhibit.

release_condition.value: both of the following have occurred: (a) Final Completion of the Subcontract Work; and (b) Contractor's receipt of retention from Owner; plus delivery of Article 10 closeout items and Article 8 waivers

evidence.quote: both of the following have occurred: (a) Final Completion of the Subcontract Work; and (b) Contractor's receipt of retention from Owner.
evidence.rationale: Section 6.2 sets the two triggers. Section 6.3 adds closeout items and waivers as a condition of release, so the clauses must be combined.

evidence.quote: Contractor shall release all retention held under this Subcontract to Subcontractor within ten (10) days after
evidence.rationale: Section 6.2 states 10 days. Exhibit C matches.

evidence.quote: With each Application for Payment, Subcontractor shall deliver a conditional waiver and release on progress payment covering the amount requested.
evidence.rationale: Section 8.1 requires a conditional progress waiver with each application.

evidence.quote: Subcontractor shall deliver an unconditional waiver and release on progress payment for the amount actually received.
evidence.rationale: Section 8.2 requires an unconditional waiver within 5 days after each payment.

evidence.quote: Subcontractor shall also obtain and deliver corresponding conditional and unconditional waivers from each of its lower-tier sub-subcontractors and material suppliers
evidence.rationale: Section 8.3 requires lower-tier waivers.

evidence.quote: shall be in the statutory forms prescribed by California Civil Code Sections 8132, 8134, 8136 and 8138, as applicable.
evidence.rationale: Section 8.4 requires the California statutory forms.

evidence.quote: Contractor may set off against any amount otherwise due to Subcontractor under this Subcontract the amount of any Backcharge.
evidence.rationale: Section 9.1 grants a setoff right for Backcharges, with written notice.

evidence.quote: Contractor may withhold from any payment an amount sufficient to cover the cost of correcting Subcontract Work that is defective or does not conform to the Subcontract Documents,
evidence.rationale: Section 9.3 permits withholding for defective work. Section 9.4 adds other grounds.

evidence.quote: Contractor will not pay for materials or equipment stored on or off the Project site that have not been incorporated into the Work.
evidence.rationale: Section 7.4 states stored materials are not payable. Exhibit C matches.

anomalies.description: The retention rate is not stated in the body of the Subcontract. Section 6.1 defers to Exhibit C, and the 5% rate appears only in that exhibit table. Confirm the exhibit is attached and executed.

evidence.quote: Contractor will withhold retention from each progress payment at the rate stated in Exhibit C.
evidence.rationale: The retention rate is not stated in the body of the Subcontract. Section 6.1 defers to Exhibit C, and the 5% rate appears only in that exhibit table. Confirm the exhibit is attached and executed.

anomalies.description: Retention release depends on Contractor's receipt of retention from Owner. Release is also conditioned on delivery of closeout items and waivers.

evidence.quote: As a condition of release, Subcontractor shall deliver the closeout items required by Article 10 and the waivers required by Article 8.
evidence.rationale: Retention release depends on Contractor's receipt of retention from Owner. Release is also conditioned on delivery of closeout items and waivers.

anomalies.description: Contractor may keep up to 150% of any disputed amount out of retention when a good faith dispute exists.

evidence.quote: an amount not exceeding one hundred fifty percent (150%) of the disputed amount until the dispute is resolved
evidence.rationale: Contractor may keep up to 150% of any disputed amount out of retention when a good faith dispute exists.

anomalies.description: Withholding for defective work continues until correction to the satisfaction of Contractor and the Architect, which is a discretionary release trigger.

evidence.quote: until the defective or nonconforming work has been corrected to the satisfaction of Contractor and the Architect.
evidence.rationale: Withholding for defective work continues until correction to the satisfaction of Contractor and the Architect, which is a discretionary release trigger.

anomalies.description: Broad additional withholding grounds include Contractor's judgment that the work cannot be completed for the unpaid balance.

evidence.quote: reasonable evidence that the Subcontract Work cannot be completed for the unpaid balance of the Subcontract Sum.
evidence.rationale: Broad additional withholding grounds include Contractor's judgment that the work cannot be completed for the unpaid balance.

anomalies.description: Backcharges include Contractor's overhead and Owner-assessed liquidated damages.

evidence.quote: liquidated damages assessed by Owner to the extent caused by Subcontractor.
evidence.rationale: Backcharges include Contractor's overhead and Owner-assessed liquidated damages.

anomalies.description: Contractor may withhold the next progress payment until the prior unconditional waiver is delivered.

evidence.quote: Contractor may withhold the next progress payment until the unconditional waiver for the prior payment has been delivered.
evidence.rationale: Contractor may withhold the next progress payment until the prior unconditional waiver is delivered.

anomalies.description: Section 7.3 says Owner nonpayment risk is not shifted to Subcontractor. However, recovery for Owner-directed changes is limited to amounts Contractor recovers from Owner, which may conflict with that statement.

evidence.quote: Subcontractor's entitlement shall be limited to the amount Contractor recovers from Owner on Subcontractor's behalf, less Contractor's reasonable costs of pursuing that recovery.
evidence.rationale: Section 7.3 says Owner nonpayment risk is not shifted to Subcontractor. However, recovery for Owner-directed changes is limited to amounts Contractor recovers from Owner, which may conflict with that statement.

anomalies.description: On Owner termination of the Prime Contract, Subcontractor's recovery is limited to what Contractor recovers from Owner.

evidence.quote: Subcontractor's recovery shall be limited to the amount Contractor recovers from Owner on account of the Subcontract Work.
evidence.rationale: On Owner termination of the Prime Contract, Subcontractor's recovery is limited to what Contractor recovers from Owner.

anomalies.description: Late applications may be deferred a full month, which extends the effective payment timing.

evidence.quote: Applications received late may be held for inclusion in the following month's application to Owner.
evidence.rationale: Late applications may be deferred a full month, which extends the effective payment timing.

anomalies.description: Acceptance of final payment waives all claims not previously reserved in writing.

evidence.quote: Acceptance of final payment by Subcontractor waives all claims by Subcontractor except those previously made in writing and identified as unsettled at the time of the final Application for Payment.
evidence.rationale: Acceptance of final payment waives all claims not previously reserved in writing.
